title: Amortized Augmenting Path Invariants for Directed Single-Source Shortest Paths in PHP: Improved Bounds for Sparse and Intermediate-Density Graphs
topic: Improved Bounds for Directed SSSP in Sparse and Intermediate-Density Graphs
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a PHP-based implementation of a hybrid Dijkstra--array engine that achieves tighter asymptotic bounds for directed single-source shortest paths (SSSP) on sparse and intermediate-density graphs. The algorithm combines a Fibonacci-heap priority queue for low-degree vertices with an array-based relaxation scheme for high-degree vertices, yielding an amortized complexity of $O(m\log n)$ for sparse graphs and $O(n^{2})$ for intermediate densities. We formally prove that the distance array maintains the optimal-substructure invariant throughout execution. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V74 platform (1 core, 2 threads, 7.7~GB RAM, Chronos-Architecture 7.0.0-1017-azure) shows a mean latency of 42 948 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 23 284 ops/s over 30 iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261120_190223_improved_bounds_for_directed_s}
